## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage

# As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups

## Problem statement

By level 5 the player has accumulated enough permanent weapon and power-up levels that they destroy enemies almost instantly, while the per-kill power-up supply is still the flat level-1 rate (18 %). Enemy density does not rise enough (and on level 5 is deliberately lower) to offset that firepower, so the mid/late campaign feels trivial and over-supplied rather than escalating.

## Users

- **Players** — "As a player, I expect each level to threaten me more than the last and to hand out fewer upgrades as I get stronger, so the campaign keeps its tension."
- **Gym users / balance engineers** — "As a balance engineer, I expect the level gym and the automated balance harness to reproduce the game's level-scaled enemy counts and drop rate, so tuning transfers to the shipped game."
- **Producers** — "As a producer, I want the change measured with before/after bot-batch evidence rather than a single hand-watched run."

## Goal

Make difficulty scale with the campaign level on two independent axes: **more enemies** and **fewer power-up drops per enemy**. Both axes are data-driven, shared with the gyms, deterministic, and evidence-backed by the automated balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Data-driven level-scaling curves** — A pure, Phaser-free shared module (proposed `src/core/levelScaling.ts`) exposes `enemyCountMultiplier(level)` and `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` backed by tunable defaults (proposed: extend `GameRules`), with inputs clamped to the campaign range. Defaults: enemy-count multiplier **1.00 at L1 → 2.00 at L10** (linear across 1–10); per-kill power-up drop chance **0.18 at L1 → 0.05 at L10** (monotonically non-increasing); the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio. Level 1 values reproduce today's behaviour exactly.
- **Enemy counts rise with level** — Campaign waves built for levels 1–10 have each group's `count` multiplied by `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`, rounded with a documented rule, floored at 1, capped by a documented per-group safety limit (≤ 200, the existing formation cap), with `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1. Level 1 wave data is byte-identical to today. The scaling applies to both the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign; same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract preserved) and the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules (AH-0MV84TE7O006HI3R).
- **Power-up supply per enemy falls with level** — Every kill-time drop roll in `PlayScene` uses the per-level chance, so the L10 per-kill drop chance is **≤ 30 % of the L1 chance**; the Extra Life roll scales proportionally. Drop types/weights and the timed weapon/power-up effects are unchanged; L1 drop behaviour is unchanged.
- **Gym parity** — The same scaling helper is used by the level-based gyms (`GymLevel`, hence `GymBotTuning`, and the curve-sequencer launch path) so a launched level produces the same enemy counts as the game, and the level-gym supply cadence is lengthened by the inverse drop-chance ratio so high-level gym runs are not over-supplied. Formation gyms keep their documented scene-specific supply source (no campaign level context) and are unchanged; the divergence is recorded in the work item and a code comment. A parity test asserts game campaign and level-gym counts match for the same level.
- **Automated balance evidence** — The deterministic evaluation harness can measure the change (extend the arena/batch so a run can exercise the real campaign waves and the real per-kill drop rule, at least for L1/L5/L10). Record a same-seed **baseline batch (100 games, competent policy)** against HEAD and a **post-change batch** in the work item or `docs/BALANCING.md`, including per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`. The evidence must show the mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the campaign remains playable (no crash, no fall in the batch's reached-level/completion metric).
- **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.
- **Documentation** — `docs/BALANCING.md` (scaling table + evidence), the GDD power-up/level sections and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (if the wave-build seam changes) are updated with the new behaviour and tuning rationale; code comments document the curves.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (repo `AGENTS.md`): enabled gameplay behaviour is shared code, consumed by the game and every relevant gym; only a documented disabled feature may diverge.
- **Determinism:** the `curve`/`fixed` wave determinism contract and same-seed reproducibility must not change.
- **Level 1 onboarding is untouched** — the multiplier and drop chance at L1 are exactly today's values, so the opening calibration, tests and balance baseline remain valid.
- **No changes to enemy archetype stats or behaviours, and no changes to the permanent weapon/power-up level economy** — this item adjusts enemy density and drop supply only. Any retuning of upgrade strength is separate scope.
- **Backwards-compatible rules persistence** — existing `localStorage` rule blobs must load with the new defaults merged in; no schema break.
- **No new player-facing UI** — the curves are tuning data, not a settings screen.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene` drops a power-up on every kill with a flat `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE = 0.18` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), plus a flat `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` (default 0.05 in `src/core/rules.ts`). Neither reads the campaign level.
- Enemy counts are hand-authored per wave in `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), merged with curve-generated waves by `buildSequencedLevels` (`src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`). `resolveCampaignLevels` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) chooses static vs sequenced. There is no level-based count multiplier anywhere.
- Level 5 is authored as "fewer enemies, structured patterns" (4–10 Phasers), while the player's permanent upgrades have accumulated — the reported over-supply peak.
- `powerUpSpawnInterval` (default 12.5 s) drives the gym supply cadence (`GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`); the game does not use it.
- The formation count cap was raised to 200 (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5), so larger scaled formations are representable.
- The automated balance harness (`src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, `docs/BALANCING.md`) simulates a single-level skirmish and **seeds** power-ups; it does not currently exercise the kill-chance drop rule or per-level campaign waves, so measuring this change needs a harness extension.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure level-scaling module with the two curves and their data defaults, clamped and documented.
2. Apply the enemy-count multiplier at the shared campaign-build seam (and the level-gym launch seam) so game and gym counts match.
3. Replace the flat kill-drop roll (and proportional Extra Life roll) in `PlayScene` with the level-resolved chance.
4. Align the level-gym supply cadence with the same curve.
5. Extend the balance harness to exercise the real campaign/drop rule and record baseline vs post-change evidence.
6. Update tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — **New.** Pure `enemyCountMultiplier`, `powerUpDropChance`, count-application helper and defaults; the single source of truth for both axes.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Add the tunable scaling data to `GameRules` with defaults, validation/clamping and backwards-compatible loading; expose defaults for tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Apply the count scaling to the campaign (both static and sequenced paths) and use the level-resolved drop chance in `_maybeDropPowerUp`; scale the Extra Life roll.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` / `src/waves/Formations.ts` — Shared seam (or a helper consumed by it) where campaign counts are scaled after composition, preserving `single` groups and determinism.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — Apply the same count scaling on launch and derive the supply cadence from the level's drop chance.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`, `src/ai/eval/types.ts`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Extend the deterministic run so campaign waves and the kill-chance drop rule participate, and the batch reports per-level evidence.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/waves/*.test.ts`, `src/core/rules.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/*.test.ts` — Curve, application, determinism, parity and harness coverage.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Scaling table, rationale and before/after evidence.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** a linear enemy-count ramp to 2.0× at L10 and a per-kill drop ramp to 0.05 are reasonable starting values; the exact values are tuning data and may be adjusted from the bot-batch evidence without changing the design.
- **Assumption:** scaling every wave (including mini-boss waves) is correct; the safety cap and formation bounds keep enlarged groups playable.
- **Risk:** doubling large formations may overflow the arena or hurt readability; mitigations are the 200-count cap, a per-wave/formation bounds test and bot-batch survival evidence.
- **Risk:** reducing drops may starve the player at levels where enemy count scaling cannot offset the loss (notably L5's small authored waves); mitigate by keeping the L5 drop chance higher than the linear endpoint and confirming with the bot batch.
- **Risk:** the evaluation harness extension is a non-trivial change to a shared tool; keep it additive (optional per-level mode) so existing batch artifacts stay compatible.
- **Risk:** `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` is an exported constant with tests/references; keep it as the documented L1 base value and derive higher levels from it so existing imports do not silently change meaning.
- **Scope-creep guard:** do not retune weapon/power-up level effects, drop weights, enemy archetypes, or the permanent-upgrade economy in this item; capture such opportunities as separate work items.
- **Documented divergence:** formation gyms have no campaign-level context, so their fixed-cadence supply stays as-is; only the level-based gyms adopt the level curve.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** (completed) — retuned the default difficulty curve and seeded campaign for playability; this item tunes the complementary enemy-density/drop-supply axis.
- **AH-0MV395QHS004SCOR** / **AH-0MVCYANT6003SG5C** (completed) — extended the campaign to 10 levels with hand-authored fixed waves; the count multiplier must preserve those authored identities.
- **AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5** (completed) — raised the formation enemy cap to 200, which makes scaled counts feasible.
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** (completed) — designed the power-up level curves (the permanent-strength side of the imbalance).
- **AH-0MV81Z2EJ006HD5T** (completed) — delivered the automated balancing batch harness that this item extends for evidence.
- **AH-0MV84TE7O006HI3R** — pure wave-balance rules (R1–R3) and audit; the scaled counts must still satisfy the campaign invariants.
- Repo `AGENTS.md` — gym↔game parity convention.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — automated balance harness and statistics schema.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5** – Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to 200 (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, everything (+15 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, get (+15 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destroying, dropped, drops, enemies, everything (+13 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should power-up supply decrease with level?** Options: (A) data-driven per-level drop-chance curve (e.g. 18 % at L1 tapering to ~5–6 % at L10) with Extra Life scaled; (B) a single global cut; (C) add a drop throttle. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. The curve is the single tunable place; Extra Life follows the same ratio.
- **Q2 — How should enemy numbers increase with level?** Options: (A) a data-driven level-based enemy-count multiplier applied when waves are built; (B) re-author static counts by hand; (C) raise only curve targets. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Applies to both fixed and curve waves and avoids re-authoring 100 waves.
- **Q3 — How should "not overpowered" be verified?** Options: (A) automated balance-evaluation evidence (bot batch: power-up pickups per run and survival trend across levels) plus unit tests for the curves; (B) deterministic unit tests only; (C) manual play-test only. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Research: the current harness seeds power-ups and plays a single-level skirmish, so this item must extend it to exercise the real campaign/drop rule for the evidence to be meaningful.

# Not all power-ups are appearing in the hull-full (hold-full) screen

> **Headline:** Restore full catalogue coverage in the hold-full choice overlay — every power-up and weapon drop (except the `reset` utility) must have a chance of appearing.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) draws its options from the static
`CHOICE_POOL` list in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, which has not kept pace with the
catalogue. Ten shipped drops never appear: the five net-new power-ups (`frenzy`,
`chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike`) and the five net-new weapons (`rear_guard`,
`broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). An exhaustive test pins the
stale 21-entry list, so the gap is invisible to the suite. All ten should have a
chance of appearing when the hold fills.

## Users

- **Player** — fills the mineral hold, opens the hold-full choice, and expects any
  power-up/weapon he has ever seen in the field (or the catalogue) to be a candidate.
  - *As a player, I want Frenzy, Chrono Field, Thorn Field, Salvage and Orbital
    Strike to be offered when my hold fills, so I can build toward the power-up
    I am collecting, rather than only ever being able to earn them as field drops.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Pool covers the full catalogue, with no gating.** `CHOICE_POOL` contains every
  power-up id (`frenzy`, `chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike` added) and every weapon id
  (`rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug` added), minus `reset`
  only, with no unlock-state filter and no per-scene copies. A regression test asserts the
  pool equals the full catalogue minus `reset`, replacing the stale exhaustive assertion in
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — New options are fully functional when picked.** Each of the ten added ids,
  selected as a base grant in the hold-full choice, applies through the existing shared
  reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward` + `effectsRegistry.applyCollect`), renders a
  name/description from the shared catalogues (`getHelpDescription`/`WEAPON_NAMES`/
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`), carries the ★ New badge when unowned, and behaves identically
  whether granted in the game (`PlayScene`) or a gym (`GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling`).
- **AC3 — Ownership/level-up offers continue to work for the new ids.** `buildChoiceCandidates`
  suppresses the base entry for an owned new item and emits its `weapon-level`/`power-up-level`
  offer with a correct `changeSummary`, for each of the ten new ids (the five weapons are
  already in `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS`; the five power-ups already have level curves).
- **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,** including code
  comments (`src/powerups/choice.ts` module prose), the GDD §4.5 pool description
  ("all power-ups plus Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc") and any affected test docs.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** The Power Pellet
  removal guard (`powerPelletRemoval.test.ts`) and the choice-strategy suite remain green,
  with the "does not over-remove" guard extended to all sixteen power-ups.

## Constraints

- **Keep the pool single-source.** The game and every gym must consume the same
  `CHOICE_POOL`/`randomChoiceStrategy`; no divergent per-scene copies (gym↔game parity,
  AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **No weighting change.** Base-entry weights stay uniform at 1.0× with the existing
  1.35× owned-upgrade bonus (Q3-A); this item fixes eligibility only. Field-drop rarity
  tuning is out of scope.
- **No unlock-state gating** (Q2-N/A): the mini-boss locked pool is being retired.
- **`reset` stays excluded** — it removes weapons rather than granting one (documented).
- **Do not touch the `unlocks.ts` machinery**; removal of the locked pool is owned by
  AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD. This item only widens the choice pool.

## Existing state

- `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) — 21 entries: 11 power-ups + 10 weapons.
- Stale exhaustive assertion in `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` pins exactly
  those 21 ids.
- The ten missing ids already exist everywhere else: `types.ts` catalogue, `rules.ts`
  weight tables (`POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS`/`WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, `defaultPowerUpWeights`/
  `defaultWeaponWeights`), `effects.ts` registry, `powerUpLevels.ts` curves, `icons.ts`,
  HUD, gym help — only the hold-full pool omits them.
- `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS` already includes the five new weapons; `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`
  already includes the five new power-ups — so level-up/ownership paths need no new code.

## Desired change

Add the ten missing ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; the pool becomes every power-up and weapon
drop id except `reset` (16 + 15 = 31 entries). Update/extend the regression tests so the
pool can never silently drift from the catalogue again, and refresh the stale docs
(choice module prose + GDD §4.5). No change to the selection strategy, weighting,
reward application, or unlock machinery.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add the ten ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; refresh module doc:
  "the base drop pool (Shield–Mineral Scoop plus the collectable weapon drops …)".
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — replace the exhaustive 21-entry assertion
  with a catalogue-derived invariant (pool ⊇ all power-up ids ∪ all weapon ids minus `reset`).
- `src/powerups/powerPelletRemoval.test.ts` — extend `REMAINING_POWER_UP_IDS` to the full
  sixteen so the "does not over-remove" guard covers the net-new power-ups.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` / `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **no change** (locked-pool
  removal is a separate item); verify only.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full pool wording ("all power-ups plus
  Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc" → full catalogue minus `reset`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` —
  consume the widened default pool automatically; verify gym tests that assert offered sets.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "hull-full screen" == the hold-full choice overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), opened when the mineral hold fills (GDD §4.5); "hull" is a
  mistyping of "hold". Confirmed by the operator's answers referencing hold-full behaviour.
- **Assumption (AC1):** the locked-pool retirement (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) will land;
  until it does, a hold-full grant of a formerly-locked weapon is acceptable (they already
  drop in the field via the weight tables).
- **Risk — widening dilutes the pool:** holding the option count at 3 while the pool grows
  from 21 → 31 makes each specific pick slightly rarer. Accepted by Q3-A (uniform
  weighting kept); rebalance is a candidate follow-up item if playtests complain.
- **Risk — gym test drift:** gym launchers inherit the widened pool automatically; tests
  asserting exact option sets may need updates — accounted for in AC2.
- **Scope creep guard:** rarity tuning for field weights, the mini-boss reward UI
  (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) and `unlocks.ts` changes are *not* part of this item.

## Related work

- AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7 — this work item.
- AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD — "Mini-Boss rewards become valuable": removes the locked-pool
  reward system; makes this item's no-gating decision stable (`related-to`).
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — "Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool": origin of
  the locked weapons now entering the pool.
- AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 / AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z — epic introducing the five net-new power-ups
  (frenzy/chrono/thorns/salvage/strike).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (single shared implementation).
- AH-0MUY47W62005FF74 / AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z — owned-upgrade 1.35× weighting (unchanged).
- AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08 — Power Pellet removal guard (must stay green).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which missing drops should enter the hold-full pool — (A) only the 5 net-new
  power-ups, or (B) the power-ups **and** the 5 mini-boss-locked weapons?"
  — Answer (operator): **B** — both categories; pool = every drop id except `reset`.
  Source: interactive reply in intake session.
  Research: `CHOICE_POOL` holds 21 ids vs 16 + 16 in the catalogue; the only missing
  weapons are the five locked ones (`reset` is a documented exclusion).
- Q2: "Should the five mini-boss-locked weapons respect the mini-boss unlock state in the
  hold-full pool?"
  — Answer (operator): **N/A** — "We are changing the mini-boss rewards system in another
  work item, there will no longer be mini-boss locked items, all powerups will be offered
  as normal powerups." Source: interactive reply. Evidence: AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD
  ("Mini-Boss rewards become valuable", open, stage `idea`) describes a wheel-based
  reward replacing the locked-pool choice; no unlock gating required here.
- Q3: "Weighting within the hold-full pool — (A) keep uniform base-entry weight, or
  (B) mirror field-drop rarity?"
  — Answer (operator): **A** — keep uniform; fix eligibility only. Source: interactive
  reply. Rationale: report is about absence, not rarity.

## How to verify

```bash
# Changed-scope gate (unit + smoke) via the project test skill:
/skill:test

# Targeted inspection while implementing:
rg -n "CHOICE_POOL" src/powerups/choice.ts
```

## Validation notes

- The ten missing ids were computed directly from the source (`types.ts` type unions vs
  `CHOICE_POOL`) — see the intake session's scripted diff (16 power-ups, 16 weapons,
  pool 21, missing `frenzy, chrono, thorns, salvage, strike` and
  `rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug`).
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search` for power-up/hold-full/keywords found no
  overlapping open item addressing pool eligibility (`discovered-from` AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD
  is a different mechanism change).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2** – Level-up offers duplicate weapon (basic + upgraded version of same weapon) (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP** – P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muy47w62005ff74, 0mv5cb6ko0079n08, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch (+329 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muy47w62005ff74, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, able, ac1 (+321 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, able, ac1, ac2 (+277 more)
